title: Guards Need Fallbacks
goal: Ensure match patterns remain exhaustive when using guards.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Pattern Matching

hints: Guard conditions must be preceded by the `if` keyword after variable binding.
The final fallback arm must be an unguarded pattern like `_` to satisfy exhaustiveness.
explanation: `x if x < 0` binds `x` and checks the guard condition. `_` provides an unguarded fallback pattern that guarantees exhaustiveness. The compiler cannot inspect guard conditions at compile time, so `_ if true` fails with `E0004` because guards are treated as potentially failing. Writing `_ if x < 0` causes `E0425` because `_` discards the value without binding `x`. Writing `x < 0` without `if` is invalid pattern syntax.
